title: World AI Conference Highlights US‑China Tech Tension
text:
The Shanghai AI conference showcases Chinese tech innovations while underscoring growing geopolitical rivalry and a looming US‑China summit on AI governance.
The World AI Conference in Shanghai brought together a mix of showcase booths, immersive demos and an undercurrent of geopolitical tension. In the bustling show hall, visitors tried Alibaba's Qwen AI glasses, a wearable that says it can read user intent and provide real‑time contextual help.
At the same time, a miniature version of the Moonshot Kimi K3 radiator‑cooling system for high‑performance GPUs was being demonstrated by a team of Chinese engineers. Even the quieter corners of the expo highlighted simple but elegant machinery: a room‑sized server rack cooled by a very cost‑effective, locally sourced system that can outpace many western designs in terms of energy efficiency.
Despite the pageantry, the underlying theme of the conference was the race between the United States and China for supremacy in AI technology and the growing need for an agreement on how to regulate it. Washington has tasked President Donald Trump with a high‑profile meeting with Chinese leader Xi Jinping later this week, the very venue where both nations will measure their technical head‑to‑head and decide if they can portray AI governance as cooperative.
